title: Rankr: choose the visual direction
question: Each direction introduces the app’s features first. Choose one to develop into a full homepage composition.

options.label: The culture edit
options.thesis: An independent culture magazine for your personal favorites.
options.viewport: A large editorial headline above five media columns, followed by an annotated ranked-list feature.
options.risk: Needs clear app previews so it never feels like a publication instead of a product.

raised.raise: A disciplined tonal scale keeps every reading surface clear.
Selected states have one unmistakable visual signal.
Asymmetry gives the central feature room to breathe.
One continuous story connects the feature sections.
One consistent icon vocabulary unites all categories.

options.label: The listening shelf
options.thesis: A personal collection of covers, rankings, and discoveries, against a quiet dark backdrop.
options.viewport: A broad feature headline paired with a ranked collection, then categories and a feature tour.
options.risk: Familiar to media-app users, so the ranking interaction must distinguish it.

options.label: The cover rack
options.thesis: An expressive cover-led catalog that invites you to build your own collection.
options.viewport: A compact feature masthead above an oversized row of covers and a feature index.
options.risk: More theatrical; cover imagery can compete with the app’s purpose.
options.case: Strong media affinity; weaker immediate feature clarity than the magazine.

options.label: Darkroom sheets
options.thesis: Layered tonal records of personal favorites.
options.risk: The photography metaphor narrows the app.
options.case: Lower audience fit and less direct feature clarity.

options.label: Signal bench
options.viewport: Ranking controls on an instrument face.
options.risk: Suggests technical measurement instead of personal taste.
options.case: Lower audience fit and task clarity.

options.label: Quiet arrangement
options.viewport: Asymmetric favorites in wide open space.
options.case: Lower media affinity and feature clarity.

options.label: Night districts
options.viewport: Media neighborhoods on a shared map.
options.risk: Implies spatial features the app does not have.
options.case: Lower audience identification and product clarity.

options.label: Collective symbols
options.thesis: A shared symbol language for personal collections.
options.case: Lower task clarity and more indirect media affinity.

canonCard.label: Familiar media-app website
canonCard.thesis: A straightforward product tour in the Beli/Letterboxd neighborhood.
canonCard.viewport: Centered introduction, app screenshot, and clear feature sections.
